failure_reason: The surge increased connections but not active execution: Threads_connected ratio_up matched, but Threads_running ratio_up 1.5 did NOT. As a result, threads_concurrency_up failed, lock_contention was only partial (waits up but wait time not), no slow_query was generated (slow_query_count_delta=0), and the system never crossed the throughput knee, so qps_ratio did not drop. Likely causes: the surge was too shallow (insufficient terminals/rate/duration), the workload wasn’t hot-spotted to induce write conflicts, and relying on traffic_surge alone may be insufficient to deterministically produce slow queries and a QPS drop.
suggested_changes: Increase concurrency to drive Threads_running ratio_up ≥ 1.5: set terminals to 480 and raise rate to ~3× baseline for at least 15 minutes to allow queues to build.

Concentrate write pressure to amplify lock wait time: skew the mix to an 80/20 hotspot on a small key range (e.g., 2 warehouses × 2 districts, remote_txn_ratio=0.0) to force intra-warehouse conflicts.
Bias the transaction mix toward write-heavy operations to raise lock contention: new_order≈50%, payment≈40%, delivery≈7%, stock_level≈2%, order_status≈1%.

Ensure the traffic generator does not throttle per-terminal too aggressively (minimize think time; raise max in-flight per terminal if applicable) so increased terminals translate into running threads.

Maintain overload long enough for slow queries to appear (slow_query_count_delta ≥ 1): run the surge for 900s; if after 300s slow_query_count is still 0, increase rate by +15–20% (e.g., to 3.5× baseline) and, if needed, terminals to 640.

To force a QPS drop (qps_ratio ≤ 0.7), keep the load above the system’s capacity knee; monitor Threads_running and InnoDB row lock wait time; if qps still doesn’t fall after 5 minutes at 3×, raise rate incrementally in 10–15% steps.

If reproducing the full chain with traffic_surge alone remains unreliable, consider adding injected_nodes (e.g., a targeted lock holder or slow_sql) in a future run to deterministically hit slow_query and qps_drop.

traffic_surge.rationale: Increase running threads by ≥1.5×, force write conflicts on hot keys to raise Innodb_row_lock_waits and lock_time_avg, create slow queries via queueing, and push the system past the throughput knee to drop QPS.

risk_warning: These changes can intentionally overload the database and create heavy write contention, potentially causing deadlocks, replication lag, long recovery/rollback, and transient unavailability. Apply only in an isolated test environment with strict safeguards (rate/terminal kill switch, CPU/disk/redo log monitoring, and timeouts). If the system exhibits sustained stalls or error spikes, immediately roll back the surge parameters.
